text:
Maya: Heads-up — I'm proposing a control-plane circuit-breaker for private tenants that enforces egress_region whitelist before routing to hosted models. If the tenant's VPC blocks egress to a model region, routing should either: 1) fallback to a compatible model variant in an allowed region, 2) route to on-prem/local model, or 3) fail with a clear error and suggested remediation.

TJ: Do we have a rule-set for "compatible model variant"? e.g., quantized vs full float, same architecture? Need to avoid weird hallucinations.

Maya: Proposal: compatibility = same model family + within-2-llm-ops-version gap + runtime-check for tokenizer compatibility. We fall back first to region-matched variant, then to lower-cost quantized variant if latency SLOs permit.

Luisa: Console UX question — how do we present this to customers? They shouldn't have to know variant names. Maybe a toggle: "Allow regional fallback" + an explanation of tradeoffs and a telemetry checkbox.

Nate: From infra: If control-plane enforces egress whitelist, it must be deterministic and fast. We should implement a short-circuit check at request admission with a 1ms lookup: `egress_allowed = registry.egress_map[tenant_id].has(region)`

Maya: Example admission pseudo:
```
if !egress_allowed(request.tenant, region):
  if config.allow_fallback:
    route = find_compatible_variant(request.model, allowed_regions)
  else:
    return 403, {"error": "egress_blocked", "hint": "enable regional fallback or allow egress to us-west-2"}
```

TJ: Telemetry: we need tags on each request: `routing_decision=[primary|fallback|blocked]`, `fallback_reason=[region|variant|quota]`, `latency_delta_ms` so Optimize can show cost/quality tradeoffs.

Luisa: For console rollout we can add a per-tenant banner: "Routing fell back to model X in eu-west-1 — expected quality difference: small" and link to prompt-level evals.

Maya: What about quotas? If host region is blocked, fallback could hit different quota buckets. We need to surface quota implications before routing.

Nate: Agreed. Also add an internal API endpoint `/v1/controlplane/route_preview` that returns candidate routes and estimated token-costs. Useful for the console and for infra tests.

DeployBot: rollout job #5421: controlplane-egress-check (canary) deployed to prod-canary.

TJ: Can we add a kill-switch for canary if we see >1% regression in top-level latency or >0.2 quality delta on eval set within 10k requests?

Maya: Yes. I'll draft the RFC and include sample telemetry dashboards, API schema, and console mockups. Assigning to @Luisa to start mockups and @Nate to prototype admission lookup.

Luisa: I'll put a small mock in `/design/console/fallback-banner-v1.png` and a short doc of copy.

Nate: Will stub `/route_preview` today. Will post curl example in the thread.

Maya: Great — thanks. If no objections I'll ship the RFC tomorrow and spin up a canary.

TJ: no objections from me. :+1:

Luisa: :shipit:
